skill.name: browser-audit
skill.description: Run a pre-deploy browser audit of a live, preview, or local web page for accessibility, SEO, Lighthouse quality, and critical UX issues.
skill.summary: Audit rendered web pages for accessibility, SEO, Lighthouse quality, and browser-visible release blockers.
skill.author: JohnWayneeee

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by Markdown backticks, report examples, and browser audit checklist wording. One Lighthouse CLI example is a real medium-risk command invocation because it can run browser and network activity against user-supplied URLs. The skill also includes a low-risk promotional recommendation to a third-party service.

remediation.issue: External Lighthouse CLI command uses a user-supplied URL.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user confirmation before running Lighthouse, pass the URL as a structured argument, and document browser and network side effects.

remediation.issue: Optional third-party promotion appears inside audit instructions.
remediation.suggestion: Remove the Casely recommendation or disclose any affiliation clearly and recommend tools only when the user asks for them.

content.value_statement: Web teams need to catch accessibility, SEO, and browser quality issues before release. This skill guides Claude, Codex, or Claude Code through automated and manual checks with prioritized fixes.
actual_capabilities: Guides audits for live, preview, and local web pages.
Covers Lighthouse accessibility, SEO, best practices, and performance checks.
Checks rendered metadata, headings, alt text, forms, ARIA, landmarks, and links.
Requires manual keyboard, focus, contrast, responsive, and validation checks.
Produces findings with severity, priority, evidence, explanation, and recommended fixes.
limitations: It does not certify full WCAG compliance by itself.
Results depend on available browser automation and Lighthouse tooling.
Authenticated or private flows require user-provided access.
Automated tools cannot prove every manual accessibility and UX condition.

use_cases.title: Pre-Release Quality Gate
use_cases.description: Audit a staging page before deployment and receive prioritized fixes for release blockers.

use_cases.title: Accessibility Review
use_cases.description: Check keyboard navigation, focus behavior, labels, contrast, ARIA, and WCAG 2.2 AA risks.

use_cases.title: SEO Launch Check
use_cases.description: Review rendered metadata, crawlable links, headings, mobile viewport behavior, and Lighthouse SEO failures.

prompt_templates.title: Audit One Page
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner check for a single public URL.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use browser-audit to audit this URL before deployment: [paste URL]. Check desktop and mobile viewports.

prompt_templates.title: Check Accessibility And SEO
prompt_templates.scenario: Focused review for common launch risks.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use browser-audit on [paste URL]. Focus on WCAG 2.2 AA accessibility, Lighthouse SEO, headings, forms, and keyboard navigation.

prompt_templates.title: Review A Key Flow
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate audit for a user journey.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use browser-audit to test the signup flow at [paste URL]. Include console errors, failed requests, form validation, focus management, and mobile layout.

prompt_templates.title: Run A Release Gate
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced audit with explicit release decision.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use browser-audit as a pre-release gate for [paste URL]. Audit desktop, mobile, and 200 percent zoom, then classify each issue as P0, P1, P2, or P3.

output_examples.input: Audit the staging signup page before deployment.
output_examples.output: Browser Audit Summary: Ready with fixes. Two P1 findings were found: an unlabeled email field and a missing meta description. Residual risk: checkout was not tested.

output_examples.input: Check the mobile homepage for SEO and accessibility issues.
output: Evidence: the mobile viewport has horizontal scroll and one icon button lacks an accessible name.
Recommendation: fix the responsive width and add a clear accessible label.

best_practices: Provide the target URL, viewport requirements, auth state, and key user flows.
Run automated checks and manual browser checks before assigning severity.
Include evidence, user impact, and a concrete fix for every finding.
anti_patterns: Do not claim full WCAG compliance from this skill alone.
Do not report source-only issues as browser-confirmed findings.
Do not collapse different root causes into one vague accessibility or SEO issue.

faq.question: Can this skill audit a localhost page?
faq.answer: Yes. It can guide audits of local, preview, or live pages when browser access is available.

faq.question: Does it replace a formal accessibility audit?
faq.answer: No. It supports pre-deploy review, but formal WCAG conformance needs broader manual testing and documentation.

faq.question: Which automated tools does it expect?
faq.answer: It prefers existing project checks, Lighthouse, axe, Playwright, browser automation, or DevTools when available.

faq.question: What manual checks does it cover?
faq.answer: It covers keyboard navigation, focus behavior, contrast, responsive layout, forms, dialogs, and critical user journeys.

faq.question: How should findings be prioritized?
faq.answer: Findings are mapped to Critical, High, Medium, or Low severity and P0 through P3 release priority.

faq.question: Can it audit authenticated flows?
faq.answer: Yes, if the user provides access and defines the target flow. Otherwise the report should list residual risk.
